title: Close the extensionless blind spot in the length cap and split boot-repair
objective: check_file_length.sh required a dot in the filename, so every extensionless executable was uncapped. boot-repair had grown to 756 lines in that gap - three times the largest capped shell file in the repo. Widen the predicate and bring the file it was hiding under the cap, without a sandbox pass that would mislead: the vmbox guest is BIOS/GRUB and this machine is UEFI.
acceptance_criteria: is_source_file() accepts extensionless files that begin with a shebang, and still skips extensionless data files such as i3/config.
Every file in the repo, including boot-repair and its new libraries, is within the 250-line cap.
The 42-test fixture suite passes with exactly the same count as before the split.
verify_shell_split.sh proves the functions moved verbatim, and any difference it reports is a deliberate change named in the evidence rather than an accident.
shellcheck is clean on the entry script and every library, with no suppression added.
No sandbox claim is made for a UEFI-critical script that a BIOS guest cannot validate.
out_of_scope: live_test.sh, which needs root and did before this change too.
Restructuring boot-repair's top-level control flow to shrink it further; the report block stays inline because sourcing it broke 30 tests.
Other extensionless scripts, all already under the cap.
verifier: check_file_length.sh --all reports boot-repair before the split and 'all checked files are within 250 lines' after; tests/test_boot_repair.sh reports 42 passed both before and after; verify_shell_split.sh reports 31/32 identical with clean_shadow_files as the one named difference; shellcheck exits 0 across the entry script and all four libs.
